questions.question: What is the angle of incidence of a ray of light falling along the normal on a glass strip?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0º**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The angle of incidence is defined as the angle between the incident ray and the normal to the surface at the point of incidence.
 
• When a ray of light falls along the normal, it means the ray is perpendicular to the surface.
 
• In this situation, the incident ray is aligned with the normal, making the angle of incidence 0º.
 
• This concept is crucial in understanding how light behaves when it strikes different surfaces, influencing reflection and refraction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Angle of Incidence**

 
 
• The angle of incidence is the angle formed by the incoming ray and the perpendicular (normal) to the surface at the point of contact.
 
• It is a fundamental concept in the study of optics, particularly in the laws of reflection and refraction.
 
• The angle of incidence is measured in degrees.
 
 
 
• **Normal Line**
 
 
• The normal line is an imaginary line perpendicular to the surface where the ray of light hits.
 
• It is used as a reference to measure angles of incidence and reflection.
 
 
 
• **Reflection and Refraction**
 
 
• **Reflection** occurs when light bounces off a surface. The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection.
 
• **Refraction** happens when light passes from one medium to another, changing its speed and direction.
 
• The relationship between the angle of incidence and refraction is described by Snell's Law.
 
 
 
• **Applications in Real Life**
 
 
• Understanding angles of incidence is crucial in designing optical devices such as lenses, mirrors, and prisms.
 
• It is also important in fields like photography, astronomy, and even in the development of various technologies like fiber optics.

questions.question: The speed of the stream is 4 km/h. A boat can cover a distance of 40 km downstream and 12 km upstream in 4 hours. Find the speed of the boat in still water (in km/h).

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For such quadratic equation problems, checking the options is the fastest method.

Total time = [Downstream distance ÷ (v + u)] + [Upstream distance ÷ (v − u)]

⇒ 40 / (v + 4) + 12 / (v − 4) = 4

⇒ 10 / (v + 4) + 3 / (v − 4) = 1

Checking Option 4: Put v = 12 ⇒ 10 / 16 + 3 / 8 = 5 / 8 + 3 / 8 = 1. (Condition is satisfied)

**∴ The correct answer is 12 km/h.**

**Given:**

Speed of stream (u) = 4 km/h

Downstream distance = 40 km

Upstream distance = 12 km

Total Time = 4 hours

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Downstream Speed = Speed of boat in still water (v) + Speed of stream (u)

Upstream Speed = Speed of boat in still water (v) − Speed of stream (u)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Time = (40 ÷ (v + 4)) + (12 ÷ (v − 4))

⇒ 4 = 40 / (v + 4) + 12 / (v − 4)

Dividing the entire equation by 4:

⇒ 10 / (v + 4) + 3 / (v − 4) = 1

⇒ [10(v − 4) + 3(v + 4)] ÷ [(v + 4)(v − 4)] = 1

⇒ 10v − 40 + 3v + 12 = v² − 16

⇒ 13v − 28 = v² − 16

⇒ v² − 13v + 12 = 0

⇒ v² − 12v − v + 12 = 0

⇒ v(v − 12) − 1(v − 12) = 0

⇒ (v − 12)(v − 1) = 0

Thus, v = 12 or v = 1.

Since the boat is able to travel upstream against a 4 km/h stream, its speed must be greater than the stream speed (v > 4).

⇒ v = 12 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 km/h.**

questions.question: If all the letters of the word ABDUCENT are arranged alphabetically, then the position of how many letters will remain unchanged?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The word given is **ABDUCENT**.
 
• When arranged alphabetically, the letters of ABDUCENT will be: **A, B, C, D, E, N, T, U**.
 
• Comparing the original positions: A (1st), B (2nd), C (3rd), D (4th), U (5th), C (6th), E (7th), N (8th), and T (9th), we find that only A and B remain in their original positions.
 
• Therefore, **2 letters** remain unchanged in their positions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alphabetical Order:**

 
 
• Alphabetical order is the sequence in which letters of the alphabet appear.
 
• For example, in alphabetical order, the sequence would be A, B, C, D, and so on up to Z.
 
 
 
• **Position in a Word:**
 
 
• The position of a letter in a word refers to its place in the sequence of letters that make up the word.
 
• For example, in the word "ABDUCENT", A is in the 1st position, B is in the 2nd position, etc.
 
 
 
• **Unchanged Position:**
 
 
• An unchanged position means that the letter remains in the same position even after the word is rearranged alphabetically.
 
• For example, if a letter is in the 1st position in both the original and the rearranged word, it is said to be in an unchanged position.

questions.question: Article 15 of the Indian Constitution deals with..........
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to equality**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 15 is part of the Right to Equality enshrined in the Indian Constitution.
 
• It prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
• Article 15(1) states that the State shall not discriminate against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth, or any of them.
 
• Article 15(2) further elaborates that no citizen shall, on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth, or any of them, be subject to any disability, liability, restriction, or condition with regard to access to shops, public restaurants, hotels, and places of public entertainment; or the use of wells, tanks, bathing ghats, roads, and places of public resort maintained wholly or partly out of State funds or dedicated to the use of the general public.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Right to Equality:**

 
 
• It is a fundamental right provided by the Constitution of India under Articles 14 to 18.
 
• Article 14 ensures equality before the law and equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
 
• Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
• Article 16 guarantees equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.
 
• Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.
 
• Article 18 abolishes titles except military and academic distinctions.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education (Article 21A):**
 
 
• It was inserted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.
 
• It mandates the State to provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of 6 to 14 years.
 
 
 
• **Right against Exploitation (Articles 23-24):**
 
 
• Article 23 prohibits human trafficking and forced labor.
 
• Article 24 prohibits the employment of children in hazardous occupations.
 
 
 
• **Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22):**
 
 
• Article 19 guarantees six freedoms to the citizens of India.
 
• Article 20 provides protection in respect of conviction for offences.
 
• Article 21 ensures the protection of life and personal liberty.
 
• Article 22 provides protection against arrest and detention in certain cases.

questions.question: A, B and C together can complete a certain work in 40 days. B and C together can complete the same work in 60 days. B is 25% more efficient than A. A, B and C work together for 30 days. In how many days will B alone complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A, B and C together can complete a certain work in 40 days.

B and C together can complete the same work in 60 days.

B is 25% more efficient than A.

A, B and C work together for 30 days.

**Formula Used:**

Work = Rate × Time

If B is 25% more efficient than A, then Efficiency_B = 1.25 × Efficiency_A

Total work = 1 unit (for simplicity)

**Calculation:**

Let Efficiency_A = A, Efficiency_B = 1.25A, Efficiency_C = C

A + B + C = 1/40 (Rate of A, B, and C together)

B + C = 1/60 (Rate of B and C together)

Substituting B = 1.25A:

⇒ B + C = 1/60

⇒ 1.25A + C = 1/60

From the first equation:

⇒ A + 1.25A + C = 1/40

⇒ 2.25A + C = 1/40

Solving the system of equations:

2.25A + C = 1/40

1.25A + C = 1/60

Subtracting the second equation from the first:

⇒ (2.25A + C) - (1.25A + C) = 1/40 - 1/60

⇒ 1A = (60 - 40) / (40 × 60)

⇒ A = 1/120

Substituting A = 1/120 into 1.25A + C = 1/60:

⇒ 1.25 × (1/120) + C = 1/60

⇒ 1/96 + C = 1/60

⇒ C = 1/60 - 1/96

⇒ C = (96 - 60) / (60 × 96)

⇒ C = 36 / 5760

⇒ C = 1/160

Now, total work completed by A, B, and C in 30 days:

Rate of A, B, and C together = 1/40

Work done in 30 days = 30 × (1/40)

Work done = 3/4

Remaining work = 1 - 3/4

Remaining work = 1/4

Efficiency of B = 1.25 × A

Efficiency of B = 1.25 × 1/120

Efficiency of B = 1/96

Days required for B to complete the remaining work:

Days = Remaining work / Efficiency of B

Days = (1/4) / (1/96)

Days = 1/4 × 96/1

Days = 24 days

**The correct answer is option 2.**

• It includes counselling, emotional support, social interaction, and community support to enhance mental well-being.
 
• During the COVID-19 pandemic, many children faced isolation, anxiety, and stress due to the disruption of their normal routines and social interactions.
 
• Psycho-social support aims to help them cope with these challenges and promote their mental health.

• Many children also faced the loss of family members, financial hardships, and lack of access to essential services.
 
• Efforts were made globally to provide support and resources to mitigate the adverse effects of the pandemic on children.

questions.question: A science textbook shows the magnetic field lines around two bar magnets labelled A and B. In A, six lines enter its south pole, and in B, three lines emerge from its north pole. The strength of A is □( ), the strength of B is □( ).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

• Since magnet A has twice the number of magnetic field lines compared to magnet B, the strength of magnet A is double that of magnet B.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnetic Field Lines**

 
 
• Magnetic field lines are a visual representation of the magnetic field around a magnet.

• The density of the magnetic field lines indicates the strength of the magnetic field.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Field Strength**
 
 
• The strength of a magnetic field is a measure of the force exerted by the magnetic field.
 
• It is proportional to the number of field lines passing through a given area.

questions.question: In the human circulatory system, all veins carry blood towards the heart. What is the difference between the pulmonary vein and other veins?

options.text: the pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood
The flow of blood in the pulmonary vein is accompanied by pressure
The pulmonary vein has a small lumen
there are no valves in the pulmonary vein

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The pulmonary vein is unique among veins because it carries **oxygenated blood** from the lungs to the left atrium of the heart.
 
• Unlike other veins, which typically carry **deoxygenated blood** from the body back to the heart, the pulmonary vein is an exception.
 
• The pulmonary vein plays a crucial role in the **pulmonary circulation** cycle, which is responsible for oxygenating blood.
 
• This oxygenated blood is then pumped out to the rest of the body by the left ventricle, ensuring the supply of oxygen to all tissues and organs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Circulatory System:**

 
 
• The human circulatory system is a complex network of the heart, blood vessels, and blood that circulates throughout the body.
 
• Its primary function is to deliver oxygen and nutrients to cells and tissues and to remove waste products.
 
• The circulatory system is divided into two main parts: the systemic circulation and the pulmonary circulation.
 
 
 
• **Pulmonary Circulation:**
 
 
• It refers to the movement of blood from the heart to the lungs and back to the heart.
 
• Deoxygenated blood is pumped from the right ventricle of the heart to the lungs via the pulmonary artery.
 
• In the lungs, carbon dioxide is exchanged for oxygen, and the now oxygenated blood is returned to the left atrium of the heart via the pulmonary veins.
 
 
 
• **Systemic Circulation:**
 
 
• This part of the circulatory system carries oxygenated blood from the left side of the heart to the rest of the body.
 
• After the tissues have used the oxygen, the deoxygenated blood returns to the right side of the heart via the veins.
 
 
 
• **Heart Chambers:**
 
 
• The heart has four chambers: two atria (upper chambers) and two ventricles (lower chambers).
 
• The right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the body and pumps it into the right ventricle, which then sends it to the lungs.
 
• The left atrium receives oxygenated blood from the lungs and pumps it into the left ventricle, which then sends it out to the body.

questions.question: According to Article 343 (1) of the Constitution of India, Hindi written in the Hindi script shall be the official language of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

questions.question: Fleming's right hand rule is used to find the direction of?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Induced current**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Fleming's right-hand rule** is used to determine the direction of the induced current when a conductor moves through a magnetic field.
 
• According to Fleming’s right-hand rule, if you stretch the thumb, forefinger, and middle finger of the right hand such that they are mutually perpendicular, the thumb represents the direction of motion of the conductor, the forefinger represents the direction of the magnetic field, and the middle finger represents the direction of the induced current.
 
• This rule is particularly useful in understanding the working of electric generators where mechanical energy is converted into electrical energy.
 
• It helps to visualize and remember the orientation of the three quantities: magnetic field, motion, and induced current, which are orthogonal to each other.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Induced Current:**

 
 
• When a conductor moves through a magnetic field, an electromotive force (EMF) is induced in the conductor, which in turn causes a current to flow if the circuit is closed. This current is called the induced current.
 
• Induced current is a result of electromagnetic induction, a fundamental principle of electromagnetism discovered by Michael Faraday.
 
 
 
• **Electromagnetic Induction:**
 
 
• Electromagnetic induction is the process by which a changing magnetic field within a conductor induces a current.
 
• This phenomenon is the working principle behind many electrical devices, such as transformers, inductors, and most types of electrical generators and motors.
 
 
 
• **Electric Field:**
 
 
• An electric field is a region around a charged particle where a force would be exerted on other charges.
 
• It is a vector field that represents the Coulomb force per unit charge exerted on a positive test charge at any point in space.
 
 
 
• **Potential:**
 
 
• Electrical potential, or voltage, is the potential energy per unit charge associated with a static electric field.
 
• It is the work needed to move a test charge from a reference point to a specific point inside the field without producing an acceleration.

questions.question: If four wires of the same material are connected like beads of a rosary, then the equivalent resistance of this rosary is □( )
questions.solution:

__
 
• When wires are connected in series, the equivalent resistance is the sum of the individual resistances.
 
• If each wire has a resistance of R, then four wires connected in series will have a total resistance of 4R.
 
• This is because the current has to pass through each resistor sequentially, adding their resistances together.
 
• The equivalent resistance being four times indicates that the resistance adds up linearly when elements are connected in series.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Resistance (R)**

 
 
• Resistance is a measure of the opposition to current flow in an electrical circuit.
 
• It is measured in ohms (Ω).
 
• Ohm's Law states that V = IR, where V is voltage, I is current, and R is resistance.
 
• Materials with high resistance are used as resistors in circuits to control current flow.
 
 
 
• **Series Connection**
 
 
• When components are connected end-to-end, they are said to be in series.
 
• In a series circuit, the current is the same through all components, but the voltage is divided among them.
 
• The total resistance in a series circuit is the sum of the individual resistances: R_total = R1 + R2 + R3 + ...
 
 
 
• **Equivalent Resistance**
 
 
• Equivalent resistance is the single resistance that can replace a group of resistances without changing the current or voltage in the circuit.
 
• For resistors in series, it is the sum of their resistances.
 
• For resistors in parallel, the reciprocal of the equivalent resistance is the sum of the reciprocals of the individual resistances: 1/R_total = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + 1/R3 + ...

questions.question: What is Virgin Vegetation?

options.text: Vegetation grown as a part of afforestation programme
A plant community that has evolved naturally without human assistance and has long been abandoned by humans
A plant community that has been cultivated with human assistance

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A plant community that has evolved naturally without human assistance and has long been abandoned by humans**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Virgin vegetation** refers to plant communities that have grown naturally without any direct or indirect human intervention.
 
• This type of vegetation develops through natural processes of succession and evolution over a long period of time.
 
• It is distinguished from other types of vegetation by the absence of human activities such as cultivation, deforestation, or any form of land use.
 
• Virgin vegetation often includes a diverse array of plant species, many of which may be endemic or specially adapted to the local environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Afforestation Programme**

 
 
• Afforestation is the process of planting trees, or sowing seeds, in a barren land devoid of any trees to create a forest.
 
• The goal is to create forests in areas where there were no trees previously, which can help combat climate change, improve air quality, and increase biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Human-Cultivated Vegetation**
 
 
• This refers to plants and trees that are deliberately grown and maintained by humans for various purposes such as agriculture, horticulture, or landscaping.
 
• Cultivated vegetation is typically managed through activities like irrigation, fertilization, and pruning.
 
 
 
• **Natural Succession**
 
 
• Ecological succession is the process by which the structure of a biological community evolves over time.
 
• Two main types of succession are primary (starting from a barren environment) and secondary (following disturbance in an area that previously had vegetation).
 
• Succession leads to a stable climax community that is in equilibrium with the environment.
 
 
 
• **Endemic Species**
 
 
• Endemic species are plants or animals that exist only in one geographic region.
 
• These species are particularly vulnerable to extinction due to their limited distribution.

questions.question: If 3 January 2006 is Tuesday, then what day of the week will be on 15 June 2010?
questions.solution:
Given: **3 January 2006** was Tuesday.

Now,

2006 to 2010 = 4 Years (3 Ordinary Years and 1 Leap Year).

And, in 4 Years = 1 Leap year and 3 Ordinary Years.

So, 1 Leap Year has 2 odd days,

And, 3 Ordinary Years have 3 odd days.

Total odd days = 2 + 3 = 5.

then, 3 January 2010 will be Tuesday + 5 = Sunday.

Now, the number of days between 3 January 2010 to 15 June 2010

= 28(Jan) + 28(Feb) + 31(Mar) + 30(Apr) + 31(May) + 15(Jun) = 163 days.

= 163 days → 163/7 = 23 weeks and 2 odd days.

So, **15 June 2010** will be Sunday + 2 = Tuesday.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

questions.question: What is the total number of single bonds in cyclopentane?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

• Cyclopentane (C₅H₁₀) is a saturated cyclic hydrocarbon with five carbon atoms.
 
• Each carbon atom forms 2 single bonds with adjacent carbon atoms and 2 single bonds with hydrogen atoms.
 
• There are a total of 5 carbon-carbon single bonds in cyclopentane.
 
• Each of the 5 carbon atoms forms 2 single bonds with hydrogen atoms, resulting in a total of 10 carbon-hydrogen single bonds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cyclopentane**

 
 
• Cyclopentane is a cyclic hydrocarbon with the molecular formula C₅H₁₀.
 
• It is a non-aromatic compound, meaning it does not have the delocalized π-electron cloud characteristic of aromatic compounds like benzene.
 
• In cyclopentane, each carbon atom is sp³ hybridized, forming four sigma (σ) bonds.
 
• The structure of cyclopentane is a five-membered ring, which can adopt conformations like envelope and half-chair to relieve angle strain.
 
 
 
• **Single Bonds**
 
 
• Single bonds are covalent bonds where two atoms share one pair of electrons.
 
• They are represented by a single line between the two atoms in chemical structures.
 
• Single bonds are sigma (σ) bonds, which are formed by the head-on overlap of atomic orbitals.
 
• In the context of hydrocarbons, single bonds can occur between carbon atoms (C-C) or between carbon and hydrogen atoms (C-H).
 
 
 
• **Saturated Hydrocarbons**
 
 
• Saturated hydrocarbons are compounds that contain only single bonds between carbon atoms.
 
• They are also known as alkanes and cycloalkanes.
 
• In saturated hydrocarbons, each carbon atom is bonded to the maximum number of hydrogen atoms possible.
 
• Examples include methane (CH₄), ethane (C₂H₆), and cyclohexane (C₆H₁₂).

questions.question: What is the method of balancing chemical equations called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Hit and trial method**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **hit and trial method **is a common and straightforward technique used to balance chemical equations. The goal is to ensure that there are the same number of each type of atom on both sides of the equation, in accordance with the Law of Conservation of Mass.
 
• This method involves adjusting the coefficients of reactants and products by trial and error until the number of atoms of each element is balanced on both sides of the equation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Molar Method**

 
 
• The Molar method involves using the mole concept to balance chemical equations.
 
• It ensures that the number of moles of each element is equal on both sides of the equation.
 
• This method is often used in stoichiometry problems.
 
• It is particularly useful for reactions involving gases where volumes are involved.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Method**
 
 
• This term is not commonly used to describe a specific method for balancing chemical equations.
 
• It may refer to any general approach used to balance chemical equations.
 
• Typically, it would involve ensuring that the number of atoms of each element is equal on both sides of the equation.
 
 
 
• **Hit and Trial Method**
 
 
• The Hit and Trial method involves trial and error to balance chemical equations.
 
• It is often used for simple equations where a systematic approach may not be necessary.
 
• This method can be time-consuming for complex equations.
 
• It involves adjusting coefficients until the number of atoms of each element is balanced on both sides of the equation.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Upper House of the Parliament of India?

options.text: It is dissolved after every 5 years.

questions.question: 12 years ago, a father was 28 years older than twice the age of his son. After how many years from now, his age will be equal to twice the age of his son?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

12 years ago, a father was 28 years older than twice the age of his son.

**Formula Used:**

Father's age 12 years ago = Son's age 12 years ago × 2 + 28

After how many years from now, Father's age = 2 × Son's age

**Calculation:**

Let the current age of the son be x years.

Father's age 12 years ago = 2(x - 12) + 28

Let the current age of the father be y years.

Since it was 12 years ago, we can write:

y - 12 = 2(x - 12) + 28

y - 12 = 2x - 24 + 28

y - 12 = 2x + 4

⇒ y = 2x + 16

After how many years from now, Father's age = 2 × Son's age?

Let the number of years be n .

After n years:

y + n = 2(x + n)

Substitute y = 2x + 16 :

2x + 16 + n = 2(x + n)

2x + 16 + n = 2x + 2n

Subtract 2x from both sides:

16 + n = 2n

Subtract n from both sides:

16 = n

**The correct answer is option 4, 16 years.**

⇒ Median − Mean = 12.06

**∴ The correct answer is 12.06.**

**__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship in Statistics

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship between mean, median, and mode is given by: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Positively Skewed Distribution

The tail of the distribution is longer on the right side. The order of central tendencies is: Mean > Median > Mode.

Negatively Skewed Distribution

The tail of the distribution is longer on the left side. The order of central tendencies is: Mean < Median < Mode.

questions.question: All of the following statements are true regarding the use of contraceptive devices except one. Choose the incorrect option.

options.text: These do not have any side effects.
They play an important role in preventing uncontrolled growth of population.
They are used to prevent or delay pregnancy.
These are used against the natural process of reproduction.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**These do not have any side effects.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Contraceptive devices can sometimes cause side effects such as nausea, weight gain, mood changes, and irregular menstrual cycles.
 
• Different types of contraceptive devices have different side effects. For example, hormonal contraceptives might cause hormonal imbalances, while intrauterine devices (IUDs) can cause discomfort or infections.
 
• It is essential to consult with a healthcare provider to choose the appropriate contraceptive method based on individual health conditions and lifestyle.
 
• Awareness and proper education about the potential side effects of contraceptive devices can help in better management and choosing the right option.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Contraceptive Devices:**

 
 
• **Hormonal Contraceptives:** These include pills, patches, injections, and hormonal IUDs. They release hormones to prevent ovulation and thicken cervical mucus to block sperm.
 
• **Barrier Methods:** These include condoms, diaphragms, and cervical caps. They physically block sperm from reaching the egg.
 
• **Intrauterine Devices (IUDs):** These are small devices inserted into the uterus. They can be hormonal or non-hormonal (copper IUDs) and prevent sperm from fertilizing the egg.
 
• **Emergency Contraceptives:** These are pills taken after unprotected sex to prevent pregnancy. They are not meant for regular use.
 
 
 
• **Natural Process of Reproduction:**
 
 
• It involves the fertilization of an egg by sperm, leading to pregnancy and the birth of offspring.
 
• Contraceptive devices interfere with this natural process to prevent or delay pregnancy.
 
 
 
• **Population Control:**
 
 
• Contraceptive devices play a crucial role in managing population growth by allowing couples to plan and space their children.
 
• They contribute to better health outcomes for women and children by reducing the risks associated with unintended pregnancies.

questions.question: The term 'geography' was coined by who among the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eratosthenes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Eratosthenes was a Greek mathematician, geographer, poet, astronomer, and music theorist.
 
• He is best known for being the first person to use the term 'geography' and for his work in geography, particularly his calculation of the Earth's circumference.
 
• He was the chief librarian at the Library of Alexandria.
 
• Eratosthenes created one of the earliest maps of the world and introduced the concept of latitude and longitude.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eratosthenes' Contributions to Geography**

 
 
• Eratosthenes is often referred to as the 'Father of Geography' for his significant contributions to the field.
 
• He invented the discipline of geography, including the terminology we still use today.
 
• One of his most famous achievements was calculating the circumference of the Earth with remarkable accuracy for his time.
 
• He also created a system of latitude and longitude, which laid the foundation for modern cartography and navigation.
 
 
 
• **Al Idrisi**
 
 
• Al Idrisi was an Arab Muslim geographer, cartographer, and Egyptologist who lived in the 12th century.
 
• He is best known for his work "Tabula Rogeriana," which is one of the most advanced medieval world maps.
 
• His work was highly influential in the medieval Islamic world and in Europe.
 
 
 
• **Ptolemy**
 
 
• Ptolemy was a Greco-Egyptian writer of Alexandria, known for his work in astronomy, mathematics, and geography.
 
• He authored the "Geographia," a comprehensive treatise on the geographical knowledge of the Greco-Roman world.
 
• Ptolemy's work influenced geographic thought for over a thousand years.
 
 
 
• **Carl Ritter**
 
 
• Carl Ritter was a German geographer who is considered one of the founders of modern geography.
 
• He emphasized the importance of empirical observation and the interrelation between human and physical geography.
 
• His work laid the groundwork for future geographical studies and education.

questions.question: Metabolic wastes are excreted by aquatic plants through □( ).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diffusion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Diffusion is the process by which molecules move from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration.
 
• It is a passive process, meaning it does not require energy expenditure from the plant.
 
• In aquatic plants, metabolic wastes such as oxygen produced during photosynthesis are removed from the cells by diffusion into the surrounding water.
 
• Diffusion allows for the efficient removal of waste products and the uptake of necessary gases like carbon dioxide for photosynthesis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Osmosis**

 
 
• Osmosis is the movement of water molecules through a semipermeable membrane from a region of lower solute concentration to a region of higher solute concentration.
 
• It is critical for maintaining cell turgidity and overall plant health.
 
• Unlike diffusion, osmosis specifically refers to the movement of water molecules.
 
 
 
• **Active Transport**
 
 
• Active transport is the movement of molecules across a cell membrane from a region of lower concentration to a region of higher concentration, using energy in the form of ATP.
 
• This process is vital for the uptake of nutrients and ions that are in lower concentrations outside the cell.
 
 
 
• **Accumulation**
 
 
• Accumulation refers to the build-up of substances within an organism or a cell.
 
• It is not a process of excretion but rather a result of an inability to effectively excrete certain substances.

• **Apex Predator:**

 
 
• An apex predator, also known as an alpha predator or top predator, is a predator at the top of a food chain, with no natural predators.
 
• Examples of apex predators include lions, wolves, sharks, and eagles.
 
• These predators play a critical role in maintaining the health of their ecosystems by controlling the population sizes of other species.
 
 
 
• **Food Chain:**

• It typically starts with a primary producer such as a plant and ends with an apex predator.
 
• Food chains are a fundamental concept in ecology, illustrating how energy and nutrients flow through an ecosystem.

questions.question: During each respiratory cycle, when air is inhaled and exhaled, there is always a certain amount of air in the lungs so that there is enough time to absorb oxygen and release carbon dioxide. What is this amount of air called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Residual amount**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The residual amount, also known as residual volume, is the volume of air remaining in the lungs after a maximal exhalation.
 
• It is crucial as it prevents the lungs from collapsing and ensures continuous gas exchange (oxygen and carbon dioxide) between breaths.
 
• This volume of air cannot be voluntarily exhaled, and it typically amounts to about 1200 ml in healthy adult males.
 
• Residual volume is essential for maintaining a consistent concentration of gases in the blood, even during different phases of the breathing cycle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Respiratory Cycle:**

 
 
• The respiratory cycle consists of inhalation and exhalation. During inhalation, air is drawn into the lungs, and during exhalation, air is expelled from the lungs.
 
• Efficient gas exchange occurs in the alveoli where oxygen from the inhaled air diffuses into the blood, and carbon dioxide from the blood diffuses into the alveoli to be exhaled.
 
 
 
• **Pulmonary Volume:**
 
 
• Various volumes of air are associated with breathing: tidal volume, inspiratory reserve volume, expiratory reserve volume, and residual volume.
 
• Tidal volume is the amount of air inhaled or exhaled during a normal breath, typically around 500 ml in adults.
 
 
 
• **Alveolar Volume:**
 
 
• The alveolar volume refers to the volume of air in the alveoli that participates in gas exchange. This is a part of the tidal volume that reaches the alveoli and is available for gas exchange.
 
• Maintaining proper alveolar volume is essential for effective oxygen and carbon dioxide exchange.

questions.question: If P, F and C represent respectively the pole, principal focus and centre of curvature of a concave mirror, then PC will be equal to.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• For a concave mirror, the distance between the pole (P) and the centre of curvature (C) is known as the radius of curvature (R).
 
• The principal focus (F) is the point where parallel rays of light either converge or appear to diverge after reflecting from the mirror.
 
• The distance between the pole (P) and the principal focus (F) is known as the focal length (f).
 
• In a concave mirror, the radius of curvature (R) is twice the focal length (f), thus PC = 2PF.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pole (P):** The pole is the geometric center of the mirror's surface. It is the point where the principal axis meets the mirror.
 
• **Principal Focus (F):** The principal focus is the point on the principal axis of a concave or convex mirror where parallel rays of light, after reflection, either converge (concave) or appear to diverge (convex).
 
• **Centre of Curvature (C):** The centre of curvature is the point on the principal axis which is the center of the sphere of which the mirror is a part. For a concave mirror, it lies in front of the mirror.
 
• **Radius of Curvature (R):** The radius of curvature is the distance between the pole (P) and the centre of curvature (C). It is twice the focal length (f) of the mirror.
 
• **Focal Length (f):** The focal length is the distance between the pole (P) and the principal focus (F). It is half of the radius of curvature (R).

questions.question: Which cells of xylem are responsible for storage of food?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parenchyma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Parenchyma cells are the only living cells in the xylem and are responsible for the storage of food.
 
• They play a crucial role in the conduction of water and nutrients in the plant.
 
• Parenchyma cells assist in the repair and regeneration of tissues, particularly in the vascular tissues.
 
• These cells are also involved in the lateral transport of water and nutrients.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• They form continuous tubes that facilitate efficient water transportation in plants.
 
• These cells have thickened cell walls reinforced with lignin, providing structural support.
 
• Vessel elements are more prominent in angiosperms (flowering plants).
 
 
 
• **Vasculature:**
 
 
• Vasculature refers to the arrangement and distribution of vascular tissues (xylem and phloem) in plants.
 
• Xylem is responsible for water and nutrient transport from roots to other parts of the plant.
 
• Phloem transports sugars and other metabolic products downwards from the leaves.
 
• The vasculature is crucial for the overall transport system within the plant body.
 
 
 
• **Xylem Fibers:**
 
 
• Xylem fibers are elongated, lignified cells that provide mechanical support to the plant.
 
• They are dead cells with thick cell walls and are typically found in the secondary xylem.
 
• Xylem fibers contribute to the strength and rigidity of the plant stem.
 
• They are not involved in water transport but play a significant role in the structural integrity of the plant.

__
 
• Mendeleev arranged elements in the periodic table based on their atomic masses and properties, not their atomic numbers.
 
• Mendeleev’s periodic table was created before the discovery of protons and neutrons, which led to the concept of atomic numbers.
 
• The modern periodic table is based on atomic numbers, which was introduced by Henry Moseley after Mendeleev's work.
 
• Mendeleev left gaps in his periodic table for undiscovered elements and predicted their properties based on periodic trends.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic Table:**

• **Atomic Number:**

• **Mendeleev’s Contributions:**
 
 
• Dmitri Mendeleev is credited with creating one of the first versions of the periodic table in 1869.
 
• He arranged the 63 known elements by increasing atomic mass and grouped them by similar chemical properties.
 
• Mendeleev predicted the existence and properties of elements that were not yet discovered, such as gallium and germanium.
 
 
 
• **Henry Moseley’s Work:**
 
 
• Henry Moseley, an English physicist, refined the periodic table by arranging elements according to their atomic numbers instead of atomic masses.
 
• Moseley's work established the modern periodic law, which states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers.

questions.question: Find the smallest four-digit number which is exactly divisible by 24, 40 and 56.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

We need to find the smallest four-digit number which is exactly divisible by 24, 40, and 56.

**Formula Used:**

Smallest number divisible by given numbers = LCM(24, 40, 56)

**Calculation:**

Prime factorization of 24: 2³ × 3

Prime factorization of 40: 2³ × 5

Prime factorization of 56: 2³ × 7

LCM = 2³ × 3 × 5 × 7

⇒ LCM = 8 × 3 × 5 × 7

⇒ LCM = 24 × 35

⇒ LCM = 840

Now, we need the smallest four-digit number divisible by 840:

Smallest four-digit number = 1000

⇒ Smallest four-digit number divisible by 840 = 840 × ceil(1000/840)

⇒ Smallest four-digit number divisible by 840 = 840 × 2

⇒ Smallest four-digit number divisible by 840 = 1680

**The smallest four-digit number which is exactly divisible by 24, 40, and 56 is 1680.**

questions.question: The Government of India Act, 1919, which contained several reforms, was passed on the basis of which of the following reports/reforms?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Government of India Act, 1919, also known as the Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms, was a significant constitutional reform enacted by the British Parliament.
 
• It introduced the concept of dyarchy, which divided the subjects of administration into two categories: transferred and reserved.
 
• The Act proposed a dual form of government for the major provinces, with elected Indian ministers accountable to the provincial legislatures.
 
• It also expanded the participation of Indians in the governance of British India by allowing a greater number of Indians to be elected to the central and provincial legislative councils.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Morley-Minto Reforms (Indian Councils Act 1909)**

 
 
• The Morley-Minto Reforms were introduced in 1909 to expand the Indian legislative councils at both the central and provincial levels.
 
• It allowed for a limited increase in the number of Indian members in the legislative councils.
 
• The reforms also introduced separate electorates for Muslims, which was a significant step towards communal representation in Indian politics.
 
 
 
• **Electoral Reform**
 
 
• Electoral reforms generally refer to changes in electoral systems to improve how public desires are expressed in election results.
 
• In the context of Indian history, electoral reforms have included measures such as the introduction of universal adult suffrage, the establishment of the Election Commission of India, and measures to ensure free and fair elections.
 
 
 
• **Dyarchy**
 
 
• Dyarchy was a system of dual government introduced by the Government of India Act, 1919.
 
• Under dyarchy, certain areas of government (the "transferred" subjects) were placed under the control of Indian ministers responsible to the legislature, while others (the "reserved" subjects) remained under the control of the British governor and his executive council.
 
• This system was intended to gradually introduce Indians to self-governance, although it was criticized for being overly complex and for not giving Indians enough real power.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Councils**
 
 
• The legislative councils were bodies at both the central and provincial levels in British India that had advisory and legislative functions.
 
• Over time, reforms such as the Indian Councils Act of 1892, the Morley-Minto Reforms, and the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms expanded their size and the role of elected Indian members.
 
• These councils were a key part of the British strategy to involve Indians in governance while maintaining ultimate control.

questions.question: Which deity is worshipped during the Hindu festival, Chhath Puja?

__
 
• Chhath Puja is a significant Hindu festival dedicated to the worship of Lord Surya (the Sun God).
 
• Lord Surya is revered as the sustainer of life and the source of energy, light, and power in the universe.
 
• During Chhath Puja, devotees perform rituals and offer prayers to Lord Surya for the well-being, prosperity, and health of their family members.
 
• The festival involves a four-day-long observance that includes holy bathing, fasting, and offering prayers and prasad (sacred food) to the Sun God.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chhath Puja**

 
 
• Chhath Puja is celebrated mainly in the Indian states of Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, and in the Madhesh region of Nepal.
 
• The festival is observed in the month of Kartika, which usually falls in October or November.
 
• Chhath Puja is also known as Surya Shashti, as it is dedicated to Lord Surya and his consort Usha (the first light of dawn).
 
• Devotees believe that by observing Chhath Puja, they can cleanse their sins and gain blessings for longevity, prosperity, and happiness.
 
• The rituals of Chhath Puja include Nahay Khay (the first day of bathing and eating pure food), Lohanda and Kharna (the second day of fasting and preparing special offerings), Sandhya Arghya (the third day of offering prayers to the setting sun), and Usha Arghya (the fourth day of offering prayers to the rising sun).
 
 
 
• **Lord Surya**
 
 
• Lord Surya is one of the principal deities in Hinduism, symbolizing the Sun.
 
• He is often depicted riding a chariot pulled by seven horses, which represent the seven colors of the rainbow and the seven days of the week.
 
• In Hindu mythology, Surya is considered the son of sage Kashyapa and Aditi, and he is also associated with various other deities such as Agni (fire) and Indra (rain).
 
• Surya is worshipped daily by many Hindus during their morning prayers, and he is also celebrated during other festivals such as Makar Sankranti and Pongal.
 
 
 
• **Other Deities Mentioned**
 
 
• **Lord Krishna:** An incarnation of Vishnu, known for his role in the epic Mahabharata and his teachings in the Bhagavad Gita.
 
• **Lord Indra:** The king of gods and the deity of rain, thunder, and lightning in Hindu mythology.

questions.question: A true-breeding tall pea plant with yellow seeds was crossed with a true-breeding dwarf pea plant with green seeds. In the F1 generation, all the plants were tall. What conclusion can be drawn from this experiment?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The experiment indicates that the tall trait is dominant over the dwarf trait in pea plants.
 
• Since all F1 generation plants were tall, it suggests that the allele for tallness masks the presence of the allele for dwarfism.
 
• True-breeding tall pea plants are homozygous for the tall allele, while true-breeding dwarf pea plants are homozygous for the dwarf allele.
 
• In the F1 generation, the genotype of the plants would be heterozygous, carrying one allele for tallness and one for dwarfism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **True-breeding**: Organisms that, when bred, produce offspring of the same variety over many generations. This indicates they are homozygous for the trait in question.
 
• **Dominant trait**: A trait that is expressed in the phenotype even when only one copy of the allele is present. In this case, tallness is dominant.
 
• **Recessive trait**: A trait that is masked by the presence of a dominant allele and only expressed phenotypically when two copies of the recessive allele are present. Here, dwarfism is recessive.
 
• **Homozygous**: An organism that has two identical alleles for a trait. True-breeding tall pea plants are homozygous dominant (TT), and true-breeding dwarf pea plants are homozygous recessive (tt).
 
• **Heterozygous**: An organism that has two different alleles for a trait. The F1 generation plants are heterozygous (Tt), having one allele for tallness and one for dwarfism.
 
• **Genotype and Phenotype**: Genotype refers to the genetic makeup of an organism, while phenotype refers to the observable traits. In this case, the genotype Tt results in the phenotype of a tall plant.

questions.question: Which of the following salts is used in black and white photography?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**AgBr**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **AgBr (Silver Bromide)** is a crucial compound used in the field of black and white photography.
 
• It is sensitive to light, which is fundamental in capturing photographic images.
 
• When exposed to light, AgBr decomposes to silver and bromine, creating a latent image that can be developed into a visible photograph.
 
• AgBr crystals are used in photographic films and papers, playing a significant role in the traditional photographic process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Photographic Process**

 
 
• The photographic process involves capturing images by exposing a light-sensitive material to light.
 
• In black and white photography, silver halides like AgBr are commonly used due to their sensitivity to light.
 
• After exposure, the film is developed using chemical solutions that reduce the silver halide to metallic silver, creating a visible image.
 
• The developed film is then fixed to remove any unexposed silver halide, ensuring the image is permanent and not sensitive to light anymore.
 
 
 
• **Silver Halides**
 
 
• Silver halides are compounds of silver with halogens (chlorine, bromine, iodine).
 
• They are used in photographic materials due to their light-sensitive properties.
 
• Common silver halides used in photography include silver bromide (AgBr), silver chloride (AgCl), and silver iodide (AgI).
 
• These compounds form the basis of traditional photographic films and papers.
 
 
 
• **Latent Image**
 
 
• A latent image is an invisible image created on a photographic film or paper after exposure to light.
 
• It is formed by the reaction of light with silver halide crystals, creating a small amount of metallic silver.
 
• The latent image is later developed into a visible image through chemical processing.
 
• This process involves amplifying the small amount of metallic silver into a visible, larger amount that forms the photograph.
 
 
 
• **Photographic Development**
 
 
• Development is a chemical process that converts the latent image into a visible image.
 
• The developer solution reduces the exposed silver halide crystals to metallic silver, forming the image.
 
• After development, the film or paper is fixed to remove unexposed silver halide, stabilizing the image.
 
• Finally, the material is washed to remove any remaining chemicals, making the photograph permanent and light-stable.

questions.question: Which chemical species is being oxidized in the following chemical reaction? CuO+H₂→Cu+H₂O
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**H₂**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the reaction CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O, hydrogen (H₂) is the species that is being oxidized.
 
• Oxidation is defined as the loss of electrons. In this reaction, H₂ loses electrons and forms H₂O.
 
• CuO is being reduced to Cu, which means it gains electrons.
 
• Oxidation and reduction always occur simultaneously in a redox reaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxidation:**

 
 
• Oxidation is a chemical reaction that involves the loss of electrons by a molecule, atom, or ion.
 
• It often involves the addition of oxygen or the removal of hydrogen.
 
• For example, in the reaction above, H₂ is oxidized to H₂O.
 
 
 
• **Reduction:**
 
 
• Reduction is the gain of electrons by a molecule, atom, or ion.
 
• It often involves the removal of oxygen or the addition of hydrogen.
 
• In the reaction above, CuO is reduced to Cu.
 
 
 
• **Redox Reactions:**
 
 
• Redox (reduction-oxidation) reactions are chemical reactions in which the oxidation states of atoms are changed.
 
• These reactions involve the transfer of electrons between two chemical species.
 
• One species gets oxidized (loses electrons), and the other gets reduced (gains electrons).
 
 
 
• **Oxidizing Agent:**
 
 
• An oxidizing agent, or oxidant, is a substance that has the ability to oxidize other substances (cause them to lose electrons).
 
• In the reaction above, CuO acts as the oxidizing agent because it accepts electrons from H₂.
 
 
 
• **Reducing Agent:**
 
 
• A reducing agent, or reductant, is a substance that has the ability to reduce other substances (cause them to gain electrons).
 
• In the reaction above, H₂ acts as the reducing agent because it donates electrons to CuO.

The correct answer is __**Option 2: i-c, ii-a, iii-b**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The pH of the human body is slightly alkaline, ranging from **7 to 7.8** (i-c).
 
• Acid rain has a pH of **less than 5.6** (ii-a).
 
• Tooth decay begins in the mouth when the pH is **less than 5.5** (iii-b).
 
• The correct matching leads to the conclusion that Option 2 is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **pH Scale:**

 
 
• The pH scale measures how acidic or basic a substance is on a scale of 0 to 14.
 
• A pH less than 7 indicates acidity, while a pH greater than 7 indicates alkalinity.
 
• A pH of 7 is considered neutral, which is the pH of pure water.
 
 
 
• **Human Body pH:**
 
 
• The human body maintains a slightly alkaline pH, typically between 7.35 and 7.45, which is crucial for various physiological processes.
 
 
 
• **Acid Rain:**
 
 
• Acid rain occurs when sulfur dioxide (SO2) and nitrogen oxides (NOx) are released into the atmosphere and react with water, oxygen, and other chemicals to form sulfuric and nitric acids.
 
• These acids then mix with rainwater, lowering its pH to below 5.6, which can harm ecosystems, buildings, and human health.
 
 
 
• **Tooth Decay and pH:**
 
 
• Tooth decay occurs when the pH in the mouth drops below 5.5, leading to the demineralization of tooth enamel.
 
• This acidic environment is often a result of bacterial metabolism of sugars present in food, producing acids that lower the pH.

Percentage = frac{{Value in 2015}}{{Value in 2021}} times 100
